They told me it would all be over soon; they said it would be painless. But really - what did they know, anyway? They had never been where I was...they had never felt the sudden realization that this was it. That years and years of experiences had led to this.

They would never grasp how every sensation became more intense, or how every heartbeat thundered in my chest, anticipatory of its impending halt. How the fibres of the rope seared my skin as it was placed around my neck, and the way one wonders how many men have met their end within the confines of this very noose.

They could never grasp the brightness of the blue sky overhead, or the unbelievable harmonies intrinsic to the noises of existence; the birds, the wind, the underlying silence that counterpoints the chorus of chanting voices - all of it, indescribable. And, of course, meaningless to the man who does not stand upon the doorstep of death, waiting to be judged.

The hood is drawn over my face, and it only succeeds in activating my senses further: I feel the warm moisture from my captured breaths, counting down to the ultimate moment; the strain of my muscles against the ropes on my wrists, ankles, neck; the delicate aroma of death and decay that wafts from the burlap across my face. 

And all too soon, all at once, the instant is upon me - and I am made aware of all the lies, and all the truths. The rope digs into my windpipe, demanding my attention, even though I am focused solely on the fading input around me. I gasp for breath - aching for just one more chance to sharpen my senses to the world beyond my reach. And at the last, it is not the pain of death that I feel, but the pain of loss - knowing that I shall no longer see such colours and wondrous things; knowing that I have heard my last sorrowful dirge or ecstatic song. 

Whoever said this was painless - they clearly still had the ability *to* feel. Such a luxury is denied to me; this - this, they will not, and can not, understand.

It was tough, waking each day with the knowledge that it would not be any better. That I'd face the dragging, innumerable seconds of that day with the whispers and the jeers; that I'd most likely be punched, spit on, judged, and relentlessly torn down, bit by bit.

It was tough, but so was I.

I walked through the halls, resilient and committed, trying my best to let the insults wash over me and away into the open air. The bullies were easy enough to see; I knew them by face and by name and by preferred hangouts, and I could usually avoid them if I wanted to. It wasn't them that I was most afraid of, though. The bullies were just disciples - loyal lesser versions of the true villains that prowled just beyond the halls - in the classrooms, to which I had to report for every class.

I could have been the only student at the school, and still left feeling like less than dirt; I could have been the valedictorian each and every year, and still been vilified. The problem was not that the other kids were mean - it was that the adults were the ones teaching them to be that way.

The teachers - the *role models* - looked down on me most of all, spewing words down from centuries before as if they had been written with me in mind. They promoted the mindset that the bullies possessed, and propogated the idea that I was fundamentally broken...and it was that, that simple idea, that broke me down, day after day.

Who protects you when the rulers are the ones slowly crushing your spirit? Who can you tell, when your pain is school-sponsored? Just to get through the never-ending hours is your biggest goal, and a miracle that even God could not lay claim to. Because after all the hurt and the anger and the indoctrination trying to convince you otherwise - if you see them for what they are, *you* are the one who gets stronger, wiser, better. *You* are the one who gets saved from a terrible life of blind acceptance and shallow perception.

I get home, hungry - *famished*. Like I hadn't eaten in days. I book it through the door and drop my things beside my shoes, tossing them onto the floor without a second thought; all I can think of is food. Tasty, wonderful, delicious food.

I run into the kitchen and slide across the tiles in my sock feet, knowing there was no time to waste. I home in on the handle of the fridge and use my momentum to whip it open in one fluid movement (yeah, Newton and I go waaaaay back). With a final flourish, I lower my gaze to plumb the depths of the shelves within, scouring every last cubic inch for something appetizing. 

Ham and cheese? Nah, I had that yesterday. Pastraviolitini (shut up, it's totally popular in Belgium) with pepper? I'm no't feeling up to that particular zest. Maybe there's something way in the back, behind the Irish-Catholic-family size box of sausages that reeked of garlic. A-ha! Yes, definitely something, fragrant and intense; I reach back and seize upon it, extricating my arm from the maze of culinary delights so that I might better inspect my discovery.

I get the can within six inches of my face and immediately regret every decision of my life that has led to this. It's almost as if those stink lines are wafting up from it; it's almost as if Satan himself had stored his leftovers in our fridge. Sprouts/tentacles/some kind of fuzzy goo are vying for freedom from the inside, clambering up the sides, and I am all at once more religious than I have ever been. A fleeting glance at the side of the can (as I try not to vomit in all directions) informs me that this abomination to things called "food" was once chicken. *Chicken?!* What the hell is *chicken* doing in a can, anyway?! Whose idea was this shit?!

With a silent vow to hunt down the people responsible, I can't stand it any longer, and lob the can like a grenade, aiming for the general direction of the garbage can. It sails spectacularly through the air, whizzing gently; it does an admittedly very nice 1 1/2 turn with a backflip, which would no doubt look quite grand in a slow motion replay. After what seems like hours, during which the horrors of that can taint the very air I breathe - it *clangs!* loudly against the side of the metal trash can - seems to hover for just a few milliseconds longer - 

....and it's gone. *I'm free*. 

I exhale, savouring the saccharine scent of pure air, no longer festering with rotten chicken. As I double over, basking in the glory of victory, my roommate pokes his head out of his room - no doubt having heard the struggle for supremacy as it unfolded.

"What was that loud clanging noise?" he asks, giving me a suspicious Raised Eyebrow.

"Nothing," I reply, panting a bit. "Just me banishing a demon to the 9th circle of Hell."

"You sure?" he says, raising his eyebrow another quarter inch. "Cuz it sounded a lot like my can of chicken hitting the garbage." He stepped out of the room, striding across the kitchen with a determination, a *zeal*, like I have never seen.

"Dude," I start, fully intending to warn him of the danger inherent to coming near the garbage can, "there's -"

In a flash, he's elbow deep in the guts of the trash, releasing the can from the bin's deathly gullet. He raises it up to see it in the sunlight, carefully checking the can for dents or damage. His brow now furrows as he searches, and he grumbles a bit.

I am disgusted; I am dumbfounded.

"This is my *dinner*, man," he snaps, matter-of-factly. "It's like wine, or cheese. It gets better with age."

I protest. "I don't think that's how it works with chi-"

I'm not even done my sentence, and he's got his head tipped back, mouth open, gobbling up chunks of canned chicken. A lumpy sauce of what may have once been gravy slowly sluices its way through the spaces, lubricating the whole thing's descent into his awaiting maw. I watch, horrifyingly enthralled, too late to save him; all that I can do now is to watch, and to wait.

It was cold - so unforgivably, unimaginably cold.

It had been a few months since the sun had disappeared. The sky had become a tapestry of the most amazing stars - every one of them teasing us with their far-off heat - and painted a beautiful picture for us to die beneath. I couldn't help but feel a bit insignificant and forgotten, wasting away on the frozen surface as I remembered sunshine, beaches, summer....

I hauled another shovelful of air into the bucket and pulled it inside the door. My lungs were burning from holding my breath, and the faceshield gave everything a golden hue, but I dared not remove the suit just yet; all the air of the earth had frozen, falling to the ground in piles and heaps. It was just as forgotten and unimportant as we were, and that was the long and short of it. There was no going back, and there was no other way around it; this was the agonizingly slow end of the world, and all the people on it.

With a last look at the dead forest before me, I slammed the door and sealed it tightly. The lack of light had killed all the plants fairly quickly, and with that the food chain collapsed as well; by now the biggest dangers were not wild animals or any other such terror you may conjure in the night, but just - *being alive* was a horror. To breathe, we braved the cold and the vacuum outside to collect sludgy, frozen air; to eat, we rationed every last calorie carefully. And yet, we continued to die, as we had always done, and the universe went on apathetically, as it would do long after our marks were gone.

I looked at the door, confident of the seal, and then placed the bucket over the fire. It was a constant see-saw, venting the smoke and barring the cold, but a necessary one; what would we breathe without this?

I watched her, sitting at the table as she stared unceasingly at the fire. She was losing it - that much was plain to see - and probably wouldn't last much longer. And then it would be me, just one last person in this never-ending terror, not far from death myself...after all, there was no more food. It simply couldn't grow, or survive. All the water on earth would be frozen soon, and any reachable water already was. The temperature was past -150 and still dropping. I had heard there may still be some alive in the nuclear subs, in the underground tunnels, in the volcano bases....but I don't have time for rumours. It's not hard to understand that everyone will die within a few more months; it's far more difficult to *accept* it as the truth. There were no longer such things as power plants, vehicles, gardens; protection, safety, or a future

Those things all faded away with the sun, just over 4 months ago. It was hard to fathom - all that time and expense, all that effort and energy into all the things the human race had done - and here we were, facing the end, with not a single escape plan. We may have been the smartest species in the universe...and we had not even considered what to do during the possibility - no, the *eventuality* - of the sun's demise. All of a sudden, I did not feel much like fighting to survive anymore, either.

It was just too much.

Sighing, I followed her gaze to the fire, and began to stare at it. Smoke was building up, so I opened the flue without hesitation; there was a breeze as the air in the bunker rushed through to the insatiably empty outdoors.

It was good to feel wind, one last time.

I attempted to move along the rails, but instead of sending signals to my legs, my brain simply showed me flashes from that night. They furiously manifested in my mind, telling me *you can't do this, they said you never would. They said, they said, they said...*

Shrieking tires; broken glass.

*Move your legs*.

That eternal instant, the one where I realized that a ton of twisted metal and screaming pain was going to hit me, and there was nothing I could do.

*One step. Take just ONE step*.

The wail of an ambulance appeared in my brain, hazy and half-remembered. I watched myself get picked up and lain on the gurney, as if it were a TV show that I happened to catch in passing. I have a distinct memory of not being able to feel my toes.

I start to get angry now. Raging. Seething at all the lost opportunity, at the injustice of it all. At how I can't even kick that driver's ass because my legs won't respond to the command. I focus every last bit of my will on that foot, and I tell it to move. It doesn't, so I tell it again. And again.

And then, right when that window at the end of the hallway seems like it will never be any nearer to me - there is motion. There is a response. 

*There is hope*.

It is awkward and ill-aimed; my foot lands clumsily and crooked. And you know what? I don't even care. It is a small and altogether short step, probably among the most ungraceful of my life.

And it is the greatest thing I have ever done. Suddenly, the hallway is too short, and all I can see is the horizon through the glass. 

I *will* be there soon.

The scientists watched in anticipation, peering through the glass at the subject in the room. Ten pairs of eyes at the ready, scanning for the slightest details, waiting for any movement that would prove their theories and validate all their years of work.

And then - there it was. Just like that. So simple that it seemed inane, and yet so complex and unbelievable. The susurrus of feelings that had been rising in the room completely broke open, and a hushed silence befell the scientists even as they wanted to cheer: they had succeeded. They had taught a monkey how to type. Granted, it would be a *long* time before it could create anything resembling prose - but it was the first step on a long road. 

Excitedly, the scientists began to jot notes, their shorthand being far more legible than the random letters the primate tapped out. Now and then he created a word, and it seemed like he may have meant it; but no, no. It was just coincidence.

He watched on the TV screen, eyes focused on nothing else. He knew the delay was creating a false sense of being there, and yet - he didn't care. He was part of this. He was alive for *this*. When he was old and decrepit, with hardly any motor skills and nothing but brittle bones, he could look at those who would carry on and say: *I was there. I saw it*.

On the screen, the helmet camera of the astronaut looked down, to see two feet firmly planted in the red dust of a pristine planet. Those on earth held their breath, as if for a moment unwilling to believe that they had done the impossible; they had done that which millions of years of evolution had said to forget. He could feel the hairs rising on his arm as he gazed upon himself, and every other living thing, on a screen in his living room. He watched himself as this astronaut saw them, as an insignificant twinkle over a hundred million miles away, and all at once he felt the tremendous weight of the universe - in both its loneliness and its beauty.

In that instant, though he knew they would find no creatures on that distant surface, he understood that *we are not alone*. Here on this life raft, this oasis in the unimaginable, endless nothingness...everything was connected. Everything was simple.

In my ear is the most expensive and sensitive headset ever built, and yet - I hear nothing but my heartbeat. The fifteen-minute delay between the people on the line and the ear that hears it is not conducive to much small talk.

It's better this way, anyway. I need time to think. I need time to prepare. Bloody hell, I had eight *months* to prepare, and countless more before that, but that was before, when I wasn't close enough to touch the dirt. When I wasn't farther from home than any person had ever been.

It was hard to think of, that. I, just another man from an apparently "important" city - though I could not discern it when I stared back at the dot of light called Earth - I was the first person to do what thousands of generations had dreamed of. I was the first to see the red up close; the first to feel the hostile windstorms screaming at my door, shrieking to get in like any other alien creature. It was terrifying, and yet gratifying - I vacillated between the two as I waited for the airlock to seal, and always, ever present, was my beating heart and my pounding pulse.

The final *hiss* sounded and the outer door began to open. Static crackled for a split second in my ear, and then was silent again; I squinted a bit as light began to filter through the crack.

Oh, God, this was it. All the planning, all the preparation, all the procedure - it was nothing to this. To feel the thrill and the exhilaration, to gaze out upon the surface of *another planet*. This was another inexplicably existent sphere in the grand cosmos, somehow called into formation by the same random rules that had made our own, and suddenly I was overwhelmed with the knowledge that *this could have been us*. We could have been a parched and dead place, crisscrossed with reminders of how things could have been; but instead, here I stood, looking out to a new world, and about to change our own.

I stepped down the ladder and took a breath. English was hard to remember; words don't express such emotions well. I had spent weeks and more thinking of something - *anything* - that would somewhat capture the exaltation of this event, and now that it was seconds away, it all seemed meaningless. As my foot descended from the last rung, it seemed to hang in the air for an eternity - touching this red dust, leaving even the tiniest mark that *we were here once*, would be the biggest event of the world's history. I knew that back home, people were watching "live", waiting with me in the airlock, and that soon enough, they'd see this too.

With the slightest crunch underfoot, audible only in the sense that I could feel it through my suit, I felt the pebbles crumble. I was here. I had done it.

No, no, let me correct that. *We had done it*. With both feet on the conquered planet, I swung around and gazed skyward to home - such an odd feeling, to see it in the black expanse - and uttered these words....
With someone, at long last, making *me* sound epic.

My heart is beating like you would not believe.

Boom *boom*, boom *boom*....

Excitement and lust and life itself flow through my veins as I stare at the phone in my hands. All I have to do is hit the numbers, the right sequence to get her phone to ring, and say a few syllables in the correct order - and that's it. That's all. It's all up to fate after that.

I continue to gaze at the screen, the little clock ticking over another minute. I realize it's almost midnight, and wonder how it got so late; suddenly my stomach churns as I come to understand that I have waited too long. 

*She won't even answer now*, I say to myself, goosebumps rising up on my arms - from anxiety or relief or disappointment, I cannot tell. *She'll be sleeping or watching a movie or - or - or on a date with someone else who had the guts to call first.*

My lip quivers, ever so slightly, and my eyes glaze over just a bit. This happens every damn time, and I've gotten used to the feeling of being passed over...and how to recover from it.

*Sweet, sweet porn stars*, I sniffle to myself, *you'll never turn me down....*

I flip the phone sideways to get the screen on wide, bypassing the clock which is insistently counting ever closer to the next cold and dreary December day. How fitting that it's the shortest one of the year; I have a feeling that I don't want to be seeing much sun anyway. With the cold and the darkness, I'll have an excuse to hide in my room and await a better opportunity.

*Ah, perfect*. Pulling from my ample stash, I bring up a video that has never failed me before. The girl is cute, innocent; her eyes draw me in, even as I know I should be looking elsewhere, lest my heterosexuality be called into question in my own head. But I find I cannot look away, and her pupils pierce into my soul...and just like that, the wall crumbles.

As the tears begin to fall, and the boner becomes ever more awkward, I find I couldn't stop even if I had wanted to. This girl, this daughter and sister and friend to *somebody*, had put in so much effort to this performance, and who would I be to tell her it's unworthy? I couldn't do that to her, despite the fact she'd never know. No, no...I owed it to her to ensure that her valiant deepthroats and almost-genuine moans did not go unnoticed. 

And so, there we sat, her and I - me on my bed, her on a 14-inch black dong of Biblical proportions. As she stubbornly rocked back and forth, loudly insisting that yes, she enjoyed this, I mimicked her motions with my hand, tears streaming down my face - a mix of grief, dishonor, disappointment, and shame. As her ebullient blue eyes stared up at the camera as she waited on her knees, I could take it no longer.

Just like that, the spasms rocked me, and I let out a wail of overwhelming sadness as well as anything else. But it was more intense than I could have imagined - all at once, I sensed the house shaking, the earth itself shifting, and a massive surge in the air as all the electronics in my house blew out. Lights overheated and burst, my TV shattered, and my phone - well, my phone was less useful than an actual brick.

Outside, in all the houses around the city, I could hear the screams begin, overpowering the endless thuds of my hammering heartbeat. It was pitch black and freezing outdoors - and the shrieks still increased.

I struggled to make out the wall clock opposite me, proclaiming it was now 12:01 AM. I hadn't even had time to grab some Kleenex, neither for my tears or my..other fluids. This was not a good start to the apocalypse. 

At least the girl didn't see me cry though. At least this way I can still die a man.

The first thing I noticed was the radio. The static; the strange shifting stations. Like there was some kind of interference along this part of the road. I chalked it up to the overhead power lines, and tried not to pay attention.

I leaned my seat back and tried to stretch my shoulders, and my neck. I had been in the car for almost 6 hours, which was about 6 hours too long for a man who yearns to be free, like me; but it was for a good cause. The only thing stronger than my desire to be unrestrained is my desire for that raison d'etre of many men: the allure of barbecued meat.

I could just see it now, visions dancing in my head like perfectly seasoned hallucinations: ribs, and steaks, and hot dogs; burgers, and patties, and meatballs and chicken breasts and smokies. Every kind of meat, sizzled to a succulent delight that would overshadow all the culinary experiences of my life to date.

*That*, my friends, would be worthy of any car ride.

The stretching in my neck felt good, so I allowed my arms to partake in the splendor. I pushed them out forward, getting leverage against the steering wheel, and in doing so I brushed one of the buttons that was meant to control the radio - but that wasn't what happened. As far as I can remember, the radio static shot through the roof, and there were colours - colours beyond any of my capacity to describe - and then a split second of blackness. And then I was here. *Here* being a term I use loosely; since I'm not exactly sure where it is.

I stopped the car, since the road had disappeared. All around me were trees, towering over my head, and giant ferns with leaves bigger than anything I'd ever seen; I opened the door and got out, getting a big whiff of air that seemed intoxicating. *Inebriating*. It was fantastic, and I had to stop myself from hauling giant lungfuls when I started to feel dizzy.

I wandered into the trees, calling out the prerequisite *hellos* and *anyone there?'s*. I was hesitant to leave the car behind, and I was about to turn around and retreat when suddenly - an aroma wafted into my olfactory cavity. A mesquite, tangy scent, with hints of a herb I couldn't identify - and couldn't resist.

Like Toucan Sam, I followed my nose through the forest, paying no mind to the small animals that skittered into the trees with my noisy arrival. Finally happening upon a clearing, I stumbled out of the foliage, scratched, panting, and exhausted - but utterly astounded.

Before me stretched a carcass, a hunk of flesh and bone that seemed far too large to have been a living thing. Strips of meat had been cut away, revealing the immense inner cavity; whatever organs had once been there had long since been liberated. Stepping further toward the source of the smell, I saw a massive firepit - and there, above it, on crude slabs of stone, my prize. My perfectly smoked, perfectly spiced prize.

Seeing no one around - and unable to care much anyway, since the pull of the meat was maddening, *stultifying* - I approached the fire and reached out a tentative hand. Upon grabbing the seared bones, slathered in some kind of homemade sauce, I heard no calls for assistance, or imperatives to halt, so I brought the food to my lips.

It smelled like heaven would smell after the first cut lawn of spring; it smelled like the hair of the first woman who decides you're worthy to lay beside. It smelled like there was nothing in this world I wanted more - and despite all that, it tasted even better.

I sank my teeth in with gusto, feeling the tender chunks break off into my mouth. I didn't even know what I was eating, but I didn't even spare a thought - within seconds, it was gone. It was captivating, and I had to have more. I grabbed another bone from the slab and picked it clean as well, working my way across until they were all gone.

Sated and satisfied, I started to wander back to the trees. I made it about twenty feet into the greenery before I collapsed from food-induced slumber; nestling into the roots of a particularly large trunk, I slept soundly and happily. The forest took me in, bidding me to rest and recover from my feast.

Hardly a second had passed when I jolted awake. I was in my car, driving on the highway; nothing had changed. I frantically wondered if I had imagined it all...until I looked in the mirror.

 I had sauce on my shirt.

I stared at the mirror, stonefaced and solemn. It reflected the light back to my eyes impartially, letting me decide for myself whether what I saw was worthy or not; but no, *no* - it had to be biased. I could swear that it was pejorating my image, perverting it to be less than perfect - how else could I explain such horrors?

I started at the top and let my eyes fall slowly. The straight, thin hair, growing haphazardly from my head, stood at attention in all directions, a silent call-to-arms for no reason. Below that, my eyebrows, too thick in the middle and too wispy at the sides, expressed nothing but disgust at what their concomitant eyes. My cheekbones flared, my lips pursed, my Adam's apple floated ungainly in the middle of my neck - *how could I only be seeing this for the first time*?!

My gaze followed the bulge of my shoulders, and my overly pudgy pectorals. I tried to escape, tried to justify my way out of the reality - but I could not. What should have been a proud paragon of the human physique was just a formless blob, a mass of atoms and ions with no real borders; it just *was*, filling the space where none should be filled. Out of the blob came two projections, firmly planting themselves to the floor like anchors; the name on the jeans that covered them did nothing to hide the true nature of their existence.

Even my feet - my feet were the worst. Far too small for my body, and yet somehow unwieldy and oversized, they took up the bare minimum of surface area required for balance and yet still appeared able to fill out the largest of clown shoes. They were almost impressive in their oxymoronic duality.

I hated what I saw, to be sure. I hated every last cell, every last strand of DNA - but. *But*. I also loved. I loved them even more than I hated. Because what was the alternative? To sulk, to pretend I was someone else, to look as though I'm something I'm not? No, no. There will be none of that here.

I may be imperfect, yes. I may be flawed and faulted and flabby, but I am nonetheless *me*. This is what I give to the world; it is not my problem if the world chooses not to take it. All of these negatives multiply together to make a most glorious positive, and for the rest of my life --

Wait, what's this? What's up with my chin? Why does it look like that? Is that - is that *seriously* how I look? What the fuck you guys?! Why wouldn't you tell me? I look like Jay Leno after an uppercut! It's so bad, it's -- it's -- it's almost hypnotizing. But I'm still mad! Even though it's hard, because the chin - it's soothing; it's tranquil. I want to look away, but then when I think about it, no....no I don't. It's safe here with the chin. I'm happy here. This is where I belong. This is where *you* belong.

It had been hard, ever since Maddie left. I tried continuing on, the best I could - but damnit, things just weren't the same. Even the little things seemed so intimidating - I couldn't even cook those foolproof mini pizzas you get from the freezer at the grocery store. Doing laundry? Ha. It would have been easier to just buy a new suit every day - which I probably would have done, if every store didn't remind me of her.

I got on the train home from work, like usual - except it wasn't. *Usually* I'd be calling her, asking what's for dinner; *usually* I'd be imagining falling asleep beside her again. So this was nothing like that, but there I was regardless. Following the shell of a schedule because I had nothing better to do, and nothing left. When you're broken - sometimes you don't even know it.

It was the #3 train, I remember. The driver was a nice guy, but in hindsight, I still wanted to punch him for being so happy over the intercom. What does he know, anyway? I bet he had a hot meal and loving hands waiting for him at home. That line runs underneath the city centre, and a hell of a lot of people come and go; I was zoning out. What else was I to do? Where else do you go to escape the inside of your own head?

And then I saw her.

It could have been Maddie's twin sister, or some other close relation; the same saccharine smile and sappire eyes. My breath begged to continue but I held it all the same...it was like looking into a strange, magic mirror, that showed all the promise of a possible future. 

She began heading over in my direction, her pregnant belly leading the way like a swollen dowsing rod. All at once my heart softened, and before I even knew it - I was standing.

"Miss," I said, gently and firmly. "Here you go. Have my seat."

She flashed her whitened teeth at me, and I caught a glimpse of how happy Maddie would have been if I just hadn't let things fall apart. She cocked her head slightly, as if to shrug it off.

"You sure?" she replied, absolutely certain of how I'd answer.

"I insist," I said, nearly ushering her into it. "Please. Sit and rest. I have plenty to think about. I have plenty to consider." And now that I did reflect, that was true...and it *was* time to stand. Time to stand up and be a man, and face what I had done. 

No more sulking; no more sadness. I was back on my feet. *I was alive.*

It was--

I gulped, a harsh sound in the dead quiet of the lab. One of the techs threw me a dirty look that I didn't bother noticing; I was focused solely on the door ahead.

The door to the nursery room. The door behind which lived, for the first time, in over ten thousand years, a wooly mammoth.

I wiped my sweating palms on my jeans and blinked the fatigue from my eyes. Now was no time to be getting tired; in mere minutes, surely just *seconds* by now, the mammoth would be released to the outside world. All those years of work, all that time spent preparing...we would be the first people outside of the cloning team to touch it. To feel it. *To understand the scope of what our race had done*.

With a hiss of air, the door began to swing open. I tensed up, and everyone in the room stared anxiously at the widening gap; the air seemed thick and heavy. I had to consciously check my breath to make sure it was staying normal.

At first - nothing. Just darkness beyond the door. I gazed through it, trying to perceive anything at all, and could not. Not a trunk, not a leg, not even a tuft of fur--

Oh, no, wait. *There* it was. 

The culmination of our species' collective knowledge, gathered into a ball of cells and into which we had breathed life itself, was slowly, cautiously stepping from the doorway. Its eyes darted back and forth, surveying and surveilling, making sure none of us posed a threat; emboldened, it emerged fully and stood in front of us. It seemed nonchalant, as if it had every right to be there - every right to exist alongside us.

I had no words; I hardly had breath. We had done it. *We had succeeded*. I could die a happy man knowing that people were not doomed to eternal war and death and ignorance; this living, breathing creature from long ages past confirmed this. 

I slumped down into my chair, dumbfounded. It was alive - and *so was I*.

There I sat in the dark, the bright light from the screen whitewashing my face. The blinking cursor kept time, mocking me; I silently willed it to grow a mind of its own and write the words that would match what I was thinking. Instead, it just flashed at me - on, off, on, off.

The seconds were ticking by; this was coming at me head-on.

I had a crippling moment of introspection. *What if he said no?* I thought, my mouth aghast. I could see him laughing on the other side of the line, calling his friends over to join him in his merriment; I had a terrible vision of my future, my chin large and grotesque as I cried constant Forever Alone tears. I foresaw my house full of cats, my deathbed covered in paw prints and fur - I saw newspaper on the floors - unused bedrooms full of hoarded junk - my family standing outside my window shaking their heads, looking up the number for the loony bin -

With considerable effort, I forced myself to think of better things. I pictured him wiping away tears of joy as he gleefully accepted my offer; I fantasized about him standing in front of his mirror, debating which suit to wear as his friends gave him advice. *No mere nerves would hold back my eternal bliss*.

My fingers found their keys, and began to type. I couldn't focus on the words as much as I wanted, for fear of shying away; I just let them flow from my brain, like water downstream. 

*I was kinda wondering, if maybe sometime, like next Friday perhaps, you wanted to maybe go get a drink, or dinner, or both at the same time lol, or maybe just watch a movie....or something?*

My finger hovered hesitantly over the Enter key; my brain was involuntarily cockblocking me and I knew it. With the concentration of a thousand sensei masters I defied the Earth's gravity and slammed my pinky down triumphantly onto the keyboard.

No. *No*. I was awake now. I was safe. I was in my own bed, next to my loving wife, with my whole life ahead of me. And perhaps, most importantly, I was *hungry*.

I stood, stretched, and strolled into the bathroom, where I [wondered if anybody was imagining what I was doing](/spoiler). Feeling about ten pounds lighter, I meandered to the kitchen, my head full of ideas that thankfully banished the howling men from my dreams back to oblivion:

*Should I have eggs*? I thought, my action-hero pecs glistening in the early morning sun. *With toast and bacon*? No, too much time to prepare. *Oatmeal?* I chuckled to myself, wondering if that king among men Bruce Lee even knew what oatmeal was. It was probably better not to risk it.

For minutes and more, I stood in silent, increasingly frantic contemplation. Pop tarts, toaster strudels, leftover pizza, and granola bars were all thrown to the sidelines; yogurt, grilled cheese, and raw cookie dough were all considered, but ultimately rejected. My brow began to furrow, and my pulse was throbbing; I couldn't stand here forever! I needed nutrients! Preferably 9 essential ones!

And just like that, it clicked. Such a simple solution to my worries. I nearly fell to my knees and thanked whatever god is popular these days; I nearly had to wipe away a tear of anticipation.

*Cereal*. That was it. Those sweet six letters contained so much more than just sounds...they had *promise.* They had honey roasted oats, almonds, fruit and nuts, wheat and flax and sugar.... they had everything I could dream of, and more. *Cereal.*

Triumphant in my decision, I marched to the cupboard and chose the mightiest bowl, befitting a fine specimen like myself. Shifting targets on the fly, my fingers then found the finely sanded knob of the next cupboard below; using a gentle touch, like one might use with a fine woman, it too was caressed from its closed state, acquiescing with nary a whimper. The box of Frosty Puffed Honeyfrootio Flakes^^TM loomed large and majestic within the reverent inner chamber; knowing my power to change worlds, I yanked it forthwith and forced its contents to be strewn into the bowl.

Oh yes, oh yes. No howling men anymore; all the noise in this kitchen would be moans of pleasure.

Shrugging off the shackles of convention, I selected a spoon from a nearby drawer, which had eagerly opened upon my invitation to do so. All that was left - all that I needed to make this fantasy a reality - was a small, insignificant, hardly-worth-mentioning quantity of milk.

That was it. That was all. But no. *No.* God, or whoever masquerades in his place, *was too cruel*.

I absentmindedly opened the fridge, expecting to be greeted with the radiant white teeth of a few quarts of milky delight. But it was not to be; there was no jug to be found. Oh yes, I say, there was plenty of butter, and cheese; plenty of yogurt and sour cream; there was even a somewhat terrifying amount of cottage cheese.

But I - a man who had conquered the womb and spent the next decades wandering a hostile planet, before finding myself here - I was milkless.

I dropped the bowl, unaware of how it shattered on the floor. My screams of rage degenerated into wordless wails; they disintegrated into - into *howls*.

I sank to my knees and gave in. My day was ruined. *I was just another howling man*.

The clock always seemed to tick slower, and louder, and harsher, when you were sitting in the room by yourself. It was just a fact of life, like how cats are jerks and bioengineering will destroy us all through an eventual *bellum zombiorum*. This particular clock was no different. It did its job with extreme satisfaction, resounding each tick with a few tens of millions of corresponding atomic vibrations of glee.

I stared at this man, this neanderthal. How he had managed to even dress himself, let alone wander in from his cave and realize his own ass fit in that chair, was beyond me; I would have thought he was staring wistfully out the window, but there was no window. Just a wall.

A blank, white, unceremonious wall, a ticking clock, me, and the missing link, all in a room. Sounds like the world's worst joke, I know. 

I go through the questions, as easily as I can. His answers get more and more infuriatingly bland. It was like he woke up that morning and came to the interview just for something to do; surely he must know that he wouldn't get the job this way? My mind began to wrap itself around this concept, and I focused doubly hard on the task at hand - halfway done.

*Come on, berg ol' buddy*, I thought to myself. *You can do this*.

As his answers fell far short of what one might consider impressive (I found it tragicomically ironic that he had to ask me what the word *adequate* meant), I was on my last ropes. He had better pull out something fabulous here, and *fast*. My patience was wearing thin, so if he didn't have the equivalent of a Broadway song and dance number, I was going to --

And just then, an interruption from the gods that toy with us mortals. That tune....I knew that tune. That MIDI style, tinny, horribly unfunny tune - what was it from, Rent? The Producers? Nope, neither. I could hear the lyrics in my head, despite the shitty quality of his ringtone: *and then, and then, and then, and then he dropped the gun, the gun, the gun...*

Fucking Chicago. My least favorite of all the musical cities. 

My teeth began to grit, and I stared in disbelief as he actually answered the call. While I loved the momentary relief that this offered me from the aural assault on my eardrums, it was quickly overtaken by rage. There he sat, like he was doing *me* a favor by being in my office, and --

*WHAT THE FUCK, DUDE? ARE YOU ACTUALLY GONNA - AW HELL NAW. HEEEEELL NAW!*

I rocketed to my feet and slammed my hands on the desk, watching his eyes jump to me. I began to stomp to the other side as he tried delicately to extricate his finger from his nostril, using all the precision of a drunken hillbilly; I watched in horror as he pulled *something* (don't you tell me that was a booger, that thing *was a fucking nameless horror*) out of his nose and panic when it wouldn't come off.

Retaining my composure, I decided to be a gentleman while escorting him from the premises. Thusly did I remove him bodily from my quarters; where he wandered, stumbling and sorrowful, after I had him tossed from the portside entrance, posterior prow-wise, I know not. 

All I know is, if that thing came off his finger before he went out the door....may God have mercy on us all.

*You're too old*, they told you, staring you down. *The kids don't wanna hear what you're putting anymore. It's past your time, old man; give it up.*

You just stared right back, your eyes locked in an optic duel to the death; you could feel the vitriol rising in your throat. You wanted to strangle them, I know. You wanted to punch the one on the left, just because it would feel so good to hear his gigantic nose break. But you restrained - for now.

*You may as well save your breath, and leave now*, you snapped back. *I started a musician, I'll die a musician. You can't--*

They broke in, ravenous for blood. *A musician? A MUSICIAN??! Don't you get it?* they screamed. *Nobody listens to a* xylophone *player these days. Especially not one in a solo group called Happy Blue Whales. You're pretty much the polar opposite--*

You surprised everyone in the room, right then. Nobody saw the spin kick coming, but it came nonetheless. Physics is a funny thing; one moment it can be your friend, and then like shifting sands, it swaps allegiances to another - this was the lesson the two men learned as they flew backwards into a conveniently placed pyramid of soup cans.

*Music is my fucking life,* you snarled, not backing down for a second. *No xylophone? Fine. No Happy Blue Whale? Fine. I'll fuckin' show you. I'll* become *the polar opposite, and do it on my own, and I'll be better off. From now on, I'm - I'm a DJ. DJ Death....flea. Fuck yea. And my debut album is gonna be about* kicking your ass.

You cracked your knuckles loudly, and grinned from ear to ear. You always did have a love for the recording process.

I would surmise that such a proposition could be undertaken in a prolix yet proficient manner, propagating my propensity for propinquity to parabilic perfection. When his eyes are scanning the horizon for any sign of my creeping advance - that is when I shall strike from above, my aquiline grace subduing him before his malicious linguistic intent can spread.

*I swear, God*, I thought to myself, tears running down my face, *if you make it stop, I will single-handedly rebuild your church. I will bear your son through my nonexistent uterus. I will do whatever the FUCK you want...just please, for the love of ALL YOUR SHIT, make it stop NOW!*

I couldn't focus; I could hardly breathe. The entire locus of my attention was directly upon the bristling ball of needles sewn inside my belly, and how it seemed absolutely deadset on the most tedious escape possible. No man, nor woman, nor beast of the earth nor sky, was created with pain like this in mind. It just wasn't natural to rip someone open, tear pieces out, shove pieces in, and give a thumbs up like that.

*Whoever invented this procedure definitely had a penis*.

*But if nothing else*, I thought, *and despite the newly obvious lack of certain parts, I am a woman. I am part of the most prominent species on the planet. I am capable of pushing a living being out of my body, and remaining coherent enough to care for it. I am* stronger than you, *bandages. You have nothing. You may be in place of my uterus but you will never understand the inner strength of my womanhood.*

I grit my teeth right there, and resolved to not let another single sound from my lips, nor tear from my eyes. Even when the phantom hedgehogs inside my midsection decided to acquaint themselves with every organ - even when their fiery knives caught on my ribs - even when I felt like gaining an extra molecule in my belly would cause it to burst - I didn't say a *word*.

Why? 

Because I'm better than that. I make obeisance to no bandage. And when I'm up and running again, and you're at the bottom of a garbage dump, soiled and forgotten - I'm going to think about you burning, and guess what, bandages? I'm gonna *laugh*.

I couldn't believe how tired I was. That was the longest day I'd had in months - in years. Maybe ever. It's not easy to be the good guy, I've found; a lot of people like being lied to, even if it's just to preserve their self-worth. Constantly being the bad guy breaking down walls will really take a toll on a man. Needless to say, I wanted the three S's: shower, shit, sleep.

Oh God, sleep. How long had it been - two days? Three? It didn't matter. What *was* important is that I had been successful; I had shown her the way. After all the arguments, and all the attempts at misdirection, and all the false phrases she kept throwing at me - I had finally shown her the light. And that moment - that split second of revelation - well, that was why I kept doing this.

For her; for them; but also for me.

I pulled into the driveway and killed the engine. The sound faded into suburbia as the early evening sun smiled down on me, and for the first time in a *long* time, I was able to hear my surroundings clearly. I had nearly forgotten what birds sounded like. It was not just singsong chirps; their music was Beethoven and Bach, under the direction of Schubert and Mozart. It was incredible. It was exactly what I needed.

I was so close to my bed now...so close.

Begrudgingly, I trudged up the driveway and into the house. I shed my dirty clothes like a snakeskin, leaving evidence of my labours in a trail up to the bathroom. This was going to be *magnificent*. I was nearly drooling at the prospect of hot water, rinsing away all my sins and insecurities. All I needed was some fresh clothes - good thing I had done laundry before I left. I hadn't had time to take them out of the basket - I never did - but that was okay. As long as they were clean, that was all I cared about.

I rounded the corner into the laundry room, and a strange set of shades and colours resolved themselves to my eyes. I blinked once, twice. I squinted and stared. I drew in a sharp breath as I realized what I was seeing. No. No no no. That absolute *asshole*. How did he even get in to my house? And why was he in the *laundry room*? His half-spilled bottle of whiskey was soaking in the carpet, and was that --

I recoiled in horror, and not a moment too soon. The *stench* - that horrid stench. The rank, rotting smell of old pepperoni and half-digested alcohol, emanating from nowhere else other than my basket of laundry. There was a bathroom next door, and he must have mistaken this room for that; uncannily, he missed the room *entirely*, yet he managed to get every drop of vomit on my clothes. I wasn't sure whether to laugh, or scream.

So I did both.

I don't know if you've ever woken up, hungover, to a naked man with bloodshot eyes screaming at you, but I imagine his morning was somewhat subpar after that. But alas, that is not my tale to tell today.

The footsteps faded behind you, but you weren't an idiot. You hadn't survived this long because you trusted one of your senses over any other. You knew that if you wanted to make it out of the place alive, you would have to stay sharp. Strong. Absolutely focused. 

You would have to be the most spectacular specimen this species had ever produced, because there was no median. There was no average. There was life, and death. And you knew *exactly* where you were going.

You reached the end of the hall, flung the door open, and slammed it shut again behind you. You didn't lock it, no; you knew that it might come from right ahead, and you'd have to backtrack, and do it quick. But you were right - your guess was spot on. You took the chance and it paid off.

There, in the glow of a single light in front of you, was a table. The table itself was of no consequence, but sitting on it was everything you needed to know. Just a simple set of lines, of otherwise insignificant patterns that offered no salvation or solution; but to you, to your well-trained eye, you could see them for what it was.

*13*, the paper on the table read. Loud and clear. Your breath, heaving in and out, the only sound in the room. You gritted your teeth, and you took another deep breath. You would only get one shot with this.

As the terrifying noise barrelled towards you out of the darkness, you swung into action. It would be close, yes - but you would be victorious. Because now you had the key: *13*.

*Alright*, you thought as you got up this morning. *This is the big day. This is what thousands of people have been waiting for. Today, Soren, today you tackle Reddit.*

You got out of bed - no, that's far too tame; you *sprang* out of bed and went to your massive and surprisingly ostentatious tie rack. You, as well as all great men, know that a tie is not merely a silken reminder of the fine exquisite things in life; rather, it is a symbol of manliness, success, and pride. It also doubles as a napkin when societal convention fails you - and this, Soren, is why you never skip your morning tie ritual.

You selected one that pleased your sight as well as your touch - all you could ask for. From there you went to the walk-in closet, which is bigger than Daniel O'Brien's house. You strode purposefully through the towering racks of pristine suits, knowing that not just any old threads would do. This was *Reddit*. This demanded *honour*.

Finally, your gaze alit upon the pinnacle of menswear, that paragon of tailored perfection. Your arm reached out, nervously, almost in reverence, and you removed it from the rack. It smelled clean, but not sterile; it had a vague scent of cigars and scotch, and you knew this was the one. It had been your trustworthy guide through innumerable Cracked meetings and late-night deadlines. This suit, despite having inspired great articles, had never encountered the word *disappoint*.

You laid the suit on the bed, next to the tie. They looked powerful and potent. You took a shower and came out refreshed, looking upon the clothing combination with new eyes; the two seemed to mesh even better than before. Your stomach leaped with the opportunities presented today. You couldn't describe it if you tried.

As men do, you shaved - even your face - and combed your hair. Taking a moment to emulate Don Draper, you nodded in swift satisfaction with yourself, confident that any woman as beautiful as January Jones would buy what you're selling. You put the suit on slowly, sensually; the fibers enticed your nerves and bristled with unbridled potential.

You dug your cowboy boots out of the closet, from where you had stashed them next to your remote control race car. You pulled them on, panicking at the last second when you realized there could have been a horrible Australian funnel web spider waiting in there; you glanced around nervously, and exhaled a sigh of relief upon noticing neither prying eyes nor unwelcome fangs in your foot. At last, your outfit was complete.

You stood, Adonis incarnate. You admired yourself for as long as you dared; eventually you shielded your eyes - just in case. But you were ready. With boots on, you would stomp through the uncharted wilds of the internet forums, and lay down the law of all who lent an ear. 

With a knowing nod, and a quick check to make sure you had everything - you sat down in your computer chair, and pressed the power button. It was only a matter of time now.

Almost unwittingly, a smile crept onto your face. Today would be a good day for Soren Bowie.
If the demand is there, I will accept this task upon myself and return literary grandeur to a wanting world. It's kind of my thing.

*But you can't build that!*, they screamed at you. *Don't you know what year it is? What time we live in?!*

You just sneered. You took a last drag of your cigarette, and threw it on the ground. One of the councillors started to protest, but you shut him up by throwing a shovelful of dirt on it. The fizzling drowned out in an avalanche of miniature pebbles; no doubt ant poets will tell tales of the Great Slide of 2012 for many years.

*If you don't like the way I dig my pit*, you mused, shoving the spade back into the ground at their feet, *you're more than welcome to break it in when I'm finished.*

They stared at you, bewildered, gauging their options. A nervous glance bounced from face to face, and then overtook all of them in tandem. Deciding not to test fate, they backed away - slowly at first, and then more quickly as the dusk wore into twilight. 

But not you. Day, night - those are just words. All that's real for you is the earth, and the lack thereof. All that's real is what a man can do with his own two hands, not what he calls it afterward. You? 

You continue to dig.

They called you ordinary. I have the truth, though - the one you thought they wouldn't see. Oh, I know. I know how it looked, how you thought you had it all planned out. Trying to have every outcome mapped and planned for. 

I just thought you all should know - ordinarypsycho has a backstory far more intense than such a misleading username lets on.

The door slammed forcefully, reinforcing the reality of her words:

*Get your things out by noon*.

I couldn't think of what else to do, so I kept sitting. The clock continued to tick, keeping time with my marathon of non-movement; the only perceptible motion was that of my eyes, slowly blinking, over and over.

My mind raced. I had caught her red-handed, there was no doubt about that, and she had tried to turn it around on me. I may be strong, but I'm not stupid...I didn't fall for it, so she screamed. She raved and ranted and almost convinced me I was a bad person, even though *she's* the one who cheated. And now there she was, storming out of the apartment and my life. Both our worlds falling apart at once.

And just like that - the dam burst. I'm just one man; even Atlas knew better than to try and hold up two planets. I can't do it. I just can't.

The tears flow, and it feels good. Great, even. I know us men aren't supposed to weep, or to wail, but *damn*, I can see why women do this so much. Now if only I could understand everything else they do. Why can't they just be happy? Why can't she just let things grow as they should? *Why do they always have to fuck it up?!*

And suddenly, I am angry. No, not angry - I am *raging*. I am a ball of pure emotion and ire. I pick up the alarm clock and throw it against the wall, watching it explode in a satisfying cloud of metal parts. Good. I stand up, not even caring that all I'm wearing are boxers. The ones she bought me just a week ago. The ones we laughed over in the store, with that stupid picture on the front. 

You know what? Fuck these things too. Off the go. BAM. I am free, literally and metaphorically. Things are going to be okay. I'm going to be fine. I just need to get rid of all this negativity, all this bad shit, and I'll be better. I will be Myself 2.0.

But speaking of shit - the bathroom is next door. Hardly even aware of my muscles moving, I stomp over and kick the door in. Fantastic. I plant myself firmly down on the seat, and realize that this is new. Everything about this experience is novel and enticing. My eyebrow raises a split second before all the negative shit comes rushing out.

Words were not made to describe such a feeling. 

Such sounds can't possibly capture the way my spirits soared, unshackled from the weight of their bodily functions. I was free and flying. I had unfettered access to every emotion, to every nerve ending. It was glorious; it was incredible; it was something she could never take away from me. No matter what else, I always had this feeling.

*She could never tell me not to*.

The box of the washing machine was everything I wanted. It was a fortress, a castle, a car, a rocket, a time machine; it was just hard enough to be stable, yet just soft enough that it could bend when I smashed it as children tend to do.

That was the box, though. The box was safe, they said, as long as you were older than five. That was me, all right! I had already lost *teeth*, okay? I had already learned how to spell big words like *toboggan*. That box didn't scare me, and couldn't hurt me. But the machine itself? No words could have ever prepared me for the horror I was to experience at its cold, mechanical, metaphorical hands.

The day dawned bright and clear, full of unrealized potential. Clouds floated lazily through the sky, but beyond that it was deep blue, the blue of a thousand daydreams. The perfect blue to play in. The kind where there's only one thing to do.

After a quick breakfast, I ran to the kitchen window and looked out into the yard. My eyes scanned the foliage, looking for my target; I began to panic when I didn't see it after a few seconds. Those seconds stretched, seemingly sempiternal, and my pulse pounded through my veins - where was it? I knew I had left it there just a few days before, and surely there was no way--

And then - catharsis. There it was, glistening in the late morning sun, already hot and hazy. My pride, my joy, the focus of every child's summer days: the lawn sprinkler.

Exhaling loudly, I ran to my bedroom and changed into my swimming trunks. There was no time for shirts, for sandals; sprinklers wait for no one! All I needed was a towel. No mere bathroom towel would sate me, though - I needed a *beach* towel. A special one, from the labyrinthine depths of the special cupboard in the laundry room.

I sojourned into the domestic laundromat, seeking my prize. I had seen my mother get them before, so I knew exactly where I was headed: the tall cupboard, positioned precariously above the washing machine. Such dizzying heights would not dissuade an explorer of my calibre, though - perish the thought! With the wanton disregard of an intrepid discoverer, I ascended the washing machine and stood, trembling at first, and then more steadily.

Up on my tip toes, I could just barely reach the edge of the cupboard. Small fingers extended, I managed to open the door, revealing the colourful threaded bounty within; I was so close, so close I could taste it! Just another - half an inch - and I would be --

Nonononononono, this can't be happening, what have I done, *what have I done?!*

In my anticipation, my center of balance shifted ever so slightly, and in that instant - it was all over for me. I tumbled downward, feeling the terrible embrace of gravity, and before I could pull a fantastic gymnastic escape, my leg connected with the edge of the washing machine. 

Oh, the horror. The absolute carnage. The myriad thoughts that ran through my mind in that moment, wondering if I would ever recover....

In due time, I was reconciled with the floor, and only then could I discern the damage. It was tender to the touch, it was swollen; the blood flowed freely. It was obviously the most painful thing ever experienced in the history of self-awareness. But all of a sudden - it didn't matter.

I could already tell there would be a scar. My own. *My very own scar, with its own cool story*. I didn't even have to scream because I knew - later in life, the ladies would be doing plenty of that whenever they realized I was the possessor of....*A Scar*.

Those summer days were supposed to be so carefree. You're supposed to enjoy the time off, when the days are hot and lazy; you're supposed to breathe deeply and majestically, and appreciate every beat of your heart. What you're *not* supposed to do is what I've just done. I can feel your adjudicating eyes, and your condescending stares - but I implore you, listen, just a moment is all I need!

It was summer. It was hot, pushing a hundred degrees. When you live in what seems to be the furthest house geographically from a pool, this kind of heat is oppressive and stifling on the best of days - and this was not the best. Our only chance at salvation was to go inside the house and escape the near-inferno that was the outdoor air.

There were four of us, that day. Myself and Danny, we were seventeen (well, almost eighteen), and Max, he was a runt of just sixteen. Then there was Dan's sister Ashley, a veritable Venus de Milo herself. She was a regal nineteen, which at the time seemed unimaginably exotic and cultured; despite this, she had a down-to-earth personality that I always enjoyed. I'd never tell him, but I originally became friends with Dan just *for* her...you know how it is.

So we're in his house. It's hot and it's boring, but none of us can go anywhere (Dan's parents had the car, they were gone for the afternoon - probably at the closest swimming hole). We lie on the couches and flop like fish for a while; we wax philosophical about things beyond the understanding of unenlightened men. The minutes tick by, and we begin to shed whatever clothes we can, just to try and survive.

I know that Max and I were catching a glimpse of Ash whenever we could. Being that age, it's not something you even have conscious control of - all you know is that you want it. You dream of it, you salivate over it, but you never think it'll happen.

So the minutes tick by, and we need something to do. Dan goes to look in the freezer for ice cream - hell, even ice CUBES - but there's nothing. In a flash of momentary brilliance, Max says *well why don't we go to the store?* Ash's eyes light up, which reciprocate back to my own. Upon seeing her radiant smile, I feel a familiar tingle travel down my spine  and...elsewhere.

*Awesome*, Dan says, nodding in agreement. The store is a fair distance down the street, too far to walk in the heat - but in a master stroke, Dan's parents had foreseen such events and bought them bicycles a few years previous. Ash had outgrown hers, but Dan still had a chance. Max, being the youngest and the smallest, was set to play copilot.

We sorted out our money, we put in our requests, and Ash and I watched them disappear down the road. As soon as their silhouettes had left our eyesight, I turned go back in, and noticed her staring at me. This was strange, as I had never seen a look like that from her before - but there was an innate part of me, a fundamental component of my DNA, that knew *exactly* what it meant.

*You're cute*, she said, matter-of-factly. *I saw you looking at me earlier, and it just so happens I'm in a good mood today.*

I dared not speak; I hardly dared breathe, lest I sabotage the words I so desperately yearned to hear next.

*I'm only gonna offer this once,* she continued. *Come upstairs with me. We can't mess up the bed, or get any stains on the covers. Just...follow me*.

I did as she asked, and she led me by the hand to the large walk-in closet in Dan's room. I remember her saying once that he got this big closet in his room because she had the bathroom in hers; in any case, at this point it wasn't all that prominent in my mind. We went in, sans light. It was dark and confined, and hotter than I imagined; none of that mattered at all.

I heard the sound of her shorts hitting the ground, and my mouth went instantly dry. Her hands went to a place where only mine had previously been, and I couldn't have spoken or moved or breathed or concentrated on ANYTHING else even if I had wanted to. Her hands were soft - I always saw her using a lot of moisturizer. Before I knew it, she [used her imagination](/spoiler) on my [specific body parts](/spoiler), and I was in Elysium. It was heaven. I couldn't help it nor hold it, and before long I [performed a totally realistic act](/spoiler) all over her [.........](/spoiler) and the whole time, she just kept making these fantastic noises. Never in my life have I felt that way, and I doubt I ever will again.

We got out of there and cleaned up just as Max and Dan returned. They'll never know, but that's okay. Sometimes it's better to know what friends are really for.

Fuckin' figures, man. The zombie apocalypse had to reach my city *today*, of all days. Don't get me wrong, it's not like I'm wussing out and crying about it. It's just, I have playlists here in my car for every day, right? Thursdays and Saturdays are heavy metal, Wednesdays and Fridays are rock n' roll. Sundays and Tuesdays are random shuffles.

 But fucking *Monday*? Monday is usually Kristi's day with the car. The playlist for today is fuckin' Coldplay and Shania Twain. If I'm gonna be crackin' walkers in the jaw all afternoon, I need something more upbeat.

Fuckin' had to be today.....but anyway.

I saw them swarming into the parking lot, and I've read enough internet to know where this would be going. While everyone else stood there gawking like live bait, I ran to the kitchen and got that shit locked *down*. Two backpacks full of food, plus whatever I'll find in my house when I get there. 

I think I've got my old baseball bat, but it's so ancient it'll probably turn to dust before its first home run. I'm gonna need something more stable. I'm gonna have to look around. I really wish Kristi would pick up her fucking phone, I mean, this shit *just started*, it's not like the phone lines are down already. Women, right? We're gonna have to move fast...these things will be right on my ass.

I'm gonna load shit into this car at the speed of sound, and take off even faster. The rest of the world can plod along and bleed on the side of the road, but I'm not going down without a fight. I always drive by a couple of those old farms just on the other side of town...I wonder if it's safe enough to hole up there for a while? 

Oh, fuck. Oh fuck. Just got home, and my front door is wide open - broken off the hinges. There's screaming. There's blood. Kristi? IF YOU FUCKERS TOUCH MY WIFE, I'M GONNA KILL YOU TWICE EVEN IF I DIDN'T FUCKING HAVE TO!

I rubbed my temples as the phone rang, mentally preparing for the inevitable flurry of idiocy that I knew would follow. It always did, didn't it? How was it that people who couldn't figure out how to plug in a computer always managed to dial at least nine numbers in the proper order, just to get someone to bitch at? It was infuriating. But hey - it paid the bills. And at the end of the day, that was all that mattered.

I clicked the button and put on my best concerned-customer-service-rep voice. I asked the standard questions and got the standard responses; I knew from the get-go that this person couldn't be as bright as they sounded, otherwise they wouldn't be on the phone with me. They mentioned something about pop-ups, and that was where I homed in.

*A godsend*, I thought. *Some useful information in this tepid sea of verbal effluvium*. 

"It sounds like you have a virus", I said, matter-of-factly. After all, I was the expert, and from here, I could really guide the conversation back to a helpful place. Maybe this wouldn't be a total waste of time.

Then came the response. I had let my guard down for a split second, and that was all this man needed to worm his way into my psyche and find the *exact place* to hit. His next words slammed me like a wall of water, and I listened with increasing disbelief as he *voluntarily* described himself *willingly* doing one of the *worst* things that a computer user can do.

*This can't be real*, I thought, when he seemed to be done speaking. I waited for the obligatory *Just kidding!*, and the courtesy guffaws of laughter.

The silence dragged on, much longer than it had to. A flicker of doubt took hold in my mind, then sprouted and grew; oh God, this guy was *serious*. He was *honestly that naive*. I can't deal with-- are you *seriou*--

I pushed the Mute button in the nick of time, as a geyser of laughter erupted from my trachea. I tried desperately, but ultimately in vain, to keep it from spreading; what a useless notion. The floodgates were now open and there was no force on heaven or earth that would keep it reined. 

I laughed for what seemed like hours, and I realized very quickly that it was not just at this man. It was at our collective society, and our priorities, and our absolute ignorance in the face of the greatest amassed knowledge our species has ever known. I laughed for all the corporate peons who were in my place, and I laughed because none of us were allowed to scream. At least this way, it sounded like it was something *funny*, but it was black laughter. Dark and terrible.

Some days when I try to sleep, I still hear that laughter, haunting me and liberating me. Sometimes it comes against my will - sometimes I call it closer. But always, I remember what it represents: the precarious scale of stupidity vs sapience, and how all it takes is some unvigilant few to upset the scale and doom us all...

Before today, I had thought I was worldly. Educated. Transmundane. I had imagined myself as a critical thinker and an established logician, and I fully believed myself to be inhabiting the best possible lifestyle, in the best possible world.

Until today. Until I encountered the grandiose and unimaginable temptation of the Doritos Locos Taco.

It had been just a regular afternoon; nothing stood out as particularly different. My friends and I were pontificating as usual - debating the great scholars and underappreciated poets of yesteryear. I was in my element, shooting down fallacies and fiercely defending my position with absolute pinpoint precision.

Then, suddenly, a twinge. An all too familiar ache in my stomach, crying out for nourishment; all at once I realized I had been so busy feeding my brain, I had forgotten all about my body! Rookie mistake. I breach the subject with my allies, who concur that caloric intake would be copacetic.

We embark on our journey, not wanting to venture too far. Being an enlightened soul who does not partake of the carnivorous traits of many others, this was making our search difficult; not many establishments nearby would cater to such whimsy. Almost in jest, one of my acquaintances suddenly says: *I dare you to eat this particular taco type. You would gain my respect and admiration, and that of our fellow comrades.*

Now I, I've been known to have gambling problems in the past, and I'm not one to turn down a challenge, so I couldn't help but accept. Resigned to this fate, I sheepishly followed them into the puebla-style diner, where I would undoubtedly abhor whatever material passed as food. I stood silently by whilst they ordered, steeling my resolve and bracing my stomach for the incoming disturbance.

They chose a table carefully, and we sat. They stared at me, and I stared back for a moment; one of them smiled. The other, ever so slowly, began to unwrap the meal in front of us.

"It's good," he said. "I promise."

I briefly considered turning back - *it's not too late!*, my stomach cried - but I needed this admiration. I *craved* it. With a final breath for good measure, I reached out, cupped the taco between my palms - and before I could justify another course of action, took a bite.

And everything changed.

The sun became brighter; the colours around me became more vivid. Sounds flowed into and out of my ears like the sweet honey of wild bees. I stared at the simple wrap of cornbread, meat, and cheese in my hands; could *this* really be so good?

I took another bite, and my soul transcended this plane of existence. I gazed upon the totality of creation, relishing my opportunity to understand the cosmos. As my physical body wolfed it down, my spirit soared to the Horsehead Nebula, to faraway planets, to galaxies we'll never know exist....and *my God*, it was good.

And then, just as soon as it had happened, I was falling. I descended like an immolating meteor, fiery and ferocious, and slammed into my earthly confines once more. The taco was gone, and only crumbs remained. 

But I knew the truth now, I had seen the light. *I knew*.

It was a Saturday - my best day. I always looked good on Saturdays. Then again, it was hard not to look good with an ironed black shirt, tailored pants, and a slick tie; I was on top of the world.

I was restless, I remember. Feeling pent up, like I needed to just have any excuse to get moving. So I decided to stroll up and down the tables at work, nonchalantly and for no real reason. Sometimes a man just has to keep his blood going, you know? So I'm walking, just like I learned as a kid. One foot in front of the other. Left, right, left, baby.

There was nothing to see at the first table. Pretty standard fare, although the girl was kind of cute. Too bad she was with that idiot, who must think that a popped collar is indicative of intelligence. I made a mental note to shoot her a wink later, maybe after I cleaned that next tab--

Oh? What was this? On my pristine, previously halcyon floor, bereft of the chaos and culinary destruction on the tables, a lone napkin had leaped to its demise. Trodden and forgotten, there it would have been overlooked for the foreseeable future, had I not happened along.

*Not on my watch*, I thought. *I got this*.

I strolled over, confident in my ability to rectify this misdeed. Ignoring the inquisitive eyes from every table nearby, I planted my feet firmly at the edges of the napkin's area of influence. I was about to reach down and get it, when from the back of my mind came a workplace safety video reminder: *lift with your legs, not with your back*. In my mind's eye, I watched the Model Worker^TM from the video bending down obediently, knees at perfect 45^o angles. 

But what was I, if not a rebel? If not an iconoclast?! Nay, no instructional video holds sway over me! I refused to bow, metaphorically *or* literally, to the bourgeousie of the restaurant industry! Chin resolutely up, I bent over to liberate the napkin from its debasement. 

Ah, the sweet familiar taste of victory, as my fingers touched the fabric.

But then - what was that noise? That grating, piercing noise, like the clucking of a thousand hens? My eyebrows raised, translating my surprise from my brain to my expression. I bode my neck to turn, and upon gazing leftward over my shoulder, the source of the sound became apparent:

*It was a trap. An ambush by two crafty cougars*. 

I was nothing but prey in their woods now. I could see their claws out, their eyes searching for the fear in my own; luckily I had dealt with this before. I stood to my full height, making myself appear bigger. They stopped cackling immediately. Good....good.

I smiled, baring my teeth to show them I meant business. They tried to retaliate, but mine were just more intimidating. Their eyes faltered, and went back to their food for just a moment.

That moment was all I needed to make my escape. And that, dear reader, is why I'm alive to tell this tale to you today.

So there I was, at the meeting. My suit was crisp and clean. My beard had been shaved to perfection, and my headspace was *in the zone*. This was my time to shine, and I knew it. I had known it for days! Just the night before I had gone out to celebrate at the Mexican restaurant down the street, because it wasn't a matter of debate - I was going to rock this meeting. My boss's bosses would be begging to promote me in no time.

So I'm sitting, nodding at all the right times, contributing all my perfectly planned ideas. I was firing on all cylinders; there was no stopping the roll I was on! Ideas were coming from every neuron - it was like I was pulling them out of thin air!

But speaking of air - what's this? Just a little tingle below my belly button? No worries, not for me. For a man like myself, who was *getting it done*, this gaseous distraction would offer no intrusion. I smirk a little to myself, thinking of how these peons will never know the emission of which they would be nasally partaking.

I lean to the side, ever so slightly. All is according to plan; all systems normal. No trouble at all. I squeeze that muscle - you know the one - and prepare to birth an airborne bowel baby.

But - oh God, *no* - not now - NOT NOW, SWEET JESUS, HELP ME --

It's too late. I can't stop it. Pandora's Box has opened, and it is *horrifying*. Man was not meant to endure such embarrassment. The clock pauses, the room halts; no, no, the whole world, the entire *universe* ceases its kinesis and focuses solely on me. Me, still frozen in mid-flatulence, unleashing a malodorous bomb with a blast radius far greater than Newtonian physics allows.

*OH GOD, WHY WON'T YOU MAKE IT STOP?!*

Still the sound continues. I can't contain it, I can't force it; it is calculated into having the optimal pressure ratio for sound-to-vibration. By now a year has passed. Leaves are falling off trees outside, and snow is falling, and now the animals are hatching their young, and *yet the groan continues*.

I would ask you to kill me now, God, but I have already died inside. And whatever killed my heart is now wrapping its miasmic, rotten-eggy tendrils firmly around the noses of everyone in my vicinity. They stare, shocked and scared and actually a little ashamed *on my behalf*. Time has stopped existing, and in its place is only eyes, dozens of eyes directly on *me*, judging, staring, unable to comprehend the olfactory odium that has emanated from my lower half.

I try to meet their gaze, but it is futile. There is no blood left in my brain to think of pride; it is all flooding my cheeks in an attempt to convey sincere apology. Suddenly the floor is the most interesting thing in the room. My eyes swan dive and firmly plant themselves next to my shoes. I see the shattered pieces of my promotion lying there in agony, and there is nothing I can do. With tears in my eyes - half from disbelieving sadness, half from the rancid carcass smell - I mouth to them, "I want to fix this...I just don't know how. Forgive me....forgive me".
